title: App Surface Auth Session Security Semantics
authority_scope: Defines cross-platform authentication, session, credential, tenant, permission-affordance, self-service, and audit semantics for app surfaces.

semantic_models.title: OIDC and OAuth client posture for mobile and web
semantic_requirements: OAuth and OIDC client posture must map authentication, authorization, permission, audit, privacy, and proof dimensions separately.
Provider integration, credentials, and live-provider evidence are execution concerns and must not be inferred from this semantic model.
Authentication readiness must not be claimed until semantic, validator, proof, and implementation gates are satisfied.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject OAuth or OIDC behaviour without semantic, permission, audit, privacy, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve client posture, requested scopes or claims, permission mapping, privacy mapping, audit mapping, and provider-mode evidence.

semantic_models.title: PKCE and native redirect URI semantics
semantic_requirements: Native redirect URI semantics must define redirect authority, callback ownership, privacy mapping, and proof expectations.
PKCE use must be treated as a proof requirement for supported native auth flows, not as implementation readiness.
Credential setup and identity provider configuration remain requires evidence.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject native auth flows without redirect URI authority, PKCE posture, permission mapping, audit mapping, privacy mapping, and proof evidence.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve native redirect URI policy, callback ownership, PKCE posture, provider mode, and audit evidence.

semantic_models.title: Web cookie session and CSRF semantics
semantic_requirements: Web session semantics must distinguish session identity, cookie policy, CSRF posture, audit, privacy, and proof.
Cookie configuration, web auth implementation, provider setup, and compliance readiness remain requires evidence.
CSRF posture must be validated against route, session, origin, and capability semantics.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject web auth behaviour without session, cookie, CSRF, audit, privacy, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve session policy, cookie policy, CSRF posture, route mapping, audit mapping, and evidence freshness.

semantic_models.title: Token refresh and revocation semantics
semantic_requirements: Token lifecycle semantics must define refresh, revocation, expiry, audit, privacy, and proof boundaries.
Token implementation and identity provider integration remain requires evidence.
Revocation semantics must fail closed when audit or proof mapping is absent.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject token lifecycle behaviour without refresh, revocation, audit, privacy, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve token lifecycle policy, revocation trigger mapping, audit evidence, privacy mapping, and provider-mode evidence.

semantic_models.title: Passkeys WebAuthn and FIDO2 posture
semantic_requirements: Passkey posture must define credential lifecycle, recovery, audit, privacy, proof, and fallback boundaries.
Passkey implementation and identity provider integration remain requires evidence.
Compliance readiness must not be inferred from passkey posture.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject passkey flows without credential lifecycle, recovery, audit, privacy, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve credential lifecycle posture, recovery posture, fallback mapping, audit evidence, and provider-mode evidence.

semantic_models.title: Biometric unlock semantics
semantic_requirements: Biometric unlock may unlock a local session context but must not redefine authorization.
Fallback and reauthentication semantics must be explicit.
Native biometric implementation, native integration, and identity provider integration remain requires evidence.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject biometric unlock without auth, audit, privacy, fallback, reauthentication, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve biometric posture, fallback mapping, reauthentication trigger mapping, local-unlock boundary, and audit evidence.

semantic_models.title: Step-up authentication model
semantic_requirements: Step-up triggers must map to governed capabilities, permission authority, risk posture, audit, privacy, and proof.
Risk provider setup and step-up implementation require the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
Security readiness must not be inferred from the presence of step-up semantics.
acceptance_confirmation: step-up triggers map to USF capability and permission authority
implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject step-up flows without capability, permission, risk, audit, privacy, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve trigger mapping, permission mapping, risk posture, audit evidence, and evidence freshness.

semantic_models.title: Tenant switching model
semantic_requirements: Tenant switching must map to tenant authority, session context, purge rules, permission checks, audit, and proof.
Tenant switching must not imply multi-tenant runtime readiness.
Implementation requires tenant, permission, purge, and audit gates exist.
acceptance_confirmation: tenant switching maps to USF tenant authority
implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject tenant switching without tenant authority, session context, purge, permission, audit, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve tenant context transition, purge evidence, permission evidence, audit evidence, and denial handling.

semantic_models.title: Role and permission mapping to UI affordances
semantic_requirements: UI affordances may reflect permissions but must not define permissions.
Denial messaging, hidden affordances, disabled affordances, audit, and proof must map back to authorization authority.
UI implementation and authorization implementation require the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
acceptance_confirmation: implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject affordances without role, permission, denial, audit, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve permission source, affordance state, denial message mapping, audit evidence, and non-claim boundary.

semantic_models.title: Account deletion export and self-service semantics
semantic_requirements: Account deletion, export, and self-service semantics must map to data governance, privacy, DSR, audit, and proof requirements.
Legal conclusions and compliance claims remain requires evidence.
Self-service implementation requires validator and proof gates exist.
acceptance_confirmation: deletion and export map to USF data governance semantics
implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject self-service flows without deletion, export, DSR, audit, privacy, dependency, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve deletion request mapping, export request mapping, DSR posture, audit evidence, evidence freshness, and non-claim boundary.

semantic_models.title: Security event and audit semantics
semantic_requirements: Security events must map to USF audit authority, privacy semantics, proof expectations, and validator checks.
Event pipeline implementation and telemetry integration remain requires evidence.
Security readiness and compliance readiness must not be inferred from event definitions.
acceptance_confirmation: security events map to USF audit authority
implementation requires the applicable bounded-local implementation gate, validator coverage, and proof evidence
semantic_models.validator_requirement: Future validators must reject security events without audit, privacy, dependency, evidence freshness, and proof mapping.
semantic_models.proof_requirement: Future proof must preserve event taxonomy, triggering authority, audit destination semantics, privacy classification, and evidence freshness.

dependency_policy.semantic_closure_meaning: Closure of the covered issues means their semantic model, validator requirement, proof requirement, dependencies, implementation gate, and non-claims are recorded.
dependency_policy.execution_claim_boundary: Closure of the covered issues does not satisfy implementation, identity provider setup, native integration, credential setup, live-provider proof, legal compliance, product UI readiness, production readiness, or security readiness.

evidence_freshness_semantics.missing: Missing evidence must not satisfy any auth, session, token, passkey, biometric, tenant, permission, self-service, audit, compliance, production, or live-provider claim.
evidence_freshness_semantics.unknown: Unknown evidence status must not satisfy pass.
evidence_freshness_semantics.stale: Stale evidence status must not satisfy pass.
evidence_freshness_semantics.generated_reports: Generated reports are lower authority than raw evidence and semantic definitions.
